newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK businesses urge restraint ahead of 97 handover.
newsitem.headline: HK businesses urge restraint ahead of 97 handover.

text.p: Hong Kong's business lobby on Monday urged the governor of the British colony, Chris Patten, to go easy on new initiatives with only 274 days left before the 1997 handover to Chinese rule.
Hong Kong will revert to Beijing's control at midnight of June 30, next year as a Special Administrative Region (SAR) of China.

"In looking to the future, we would like to urge restraint, with little in the way of new initiatives which might prove difficult for the new SAR chief executive and government to implement," the Hong Kong General Chamber of Commerce said in a statement.

"We would prefer to see an emphasis on the need for cooperation with the Chinese authorities and SAR government team-designate and the completion of necessary tasks ahead of the handover on July 1," it added.

The statement was in response to a report in the South China Morning Post, which said Patten, the 28th and the last British governor of Hong Kong, would announce hundreds of new initiatives in his last policy address on Wednesday.
The newspaper quoted sources as saying Patten wanted to reject any allegation of a lame duck government.
